svg.text: ESP32-DevKitC pin map: the console's screen, knob, chip and buttons
Seen from the top, antenna up, USB at the bottom. Header J2 runs down the left, J3 down the right, pin 1 at the top. Names as printed on the board.
A 30-pin board (DOIT DevKit V1) has the same GPIOs in another order, some printed D23 for IO23: wire by the names, not by position.
3.3 V: screen 3V3, chip VIN (by the rails)
Sign button: A, held to sign
boot pin: never high at power-up
ground: knob C and SW2, buttons (by the rails)
Reject button: Y, and Wi-Fi setup at power-up
free here; PSRAM on a WROVER
free here; PSRAM on a WROVER
boot pin; the LED on some boards
Why these pins, and the rules
1. Everything runs on 3.3 V from the 3V3 pin. The 5V pin is the USB's 5 V: nothing goes there.
2. Never D0-D3, CMD or CLK (GPIO 6-11): they are the module's flash, and the board stops.
3. The screen's clock and data are on VSPI's own pins, IO18 and IO23, so firmware drives them as SPI(2) at full speed.
4. Boot pins: IO0 (the BOOT button), IO2 and IO12 decide how the ESP32 starts. Nothing here pulls them. CS (IO5) and RST (IO15) are
boot pins too, but both rest high, which is what the ESP32 wants at power-up.
5. IO16 and IO17 are free on a WROOM-32 but hold the PSRAM on a WROVER, so this map leaves them alone: the same wires work on both.
6. IO34-39 (and VP, VN) are inputs with no pull-ups: no knob or button there. The knob and buttons use the ESP32's own pull-ups.
7. The chip only gets read on the bench. Locking an ATECC608 is permanent (docs/LOCKING.md).
